scope: Independent historical identity and scope assessment, not a fresh audit of every existing Roman Republic passage.
conclusion: The two imported labels represent interleaved coverage of the Roman republican state. A shared card is historically justified. Association does not authenticate every imported territorial edge and does not include Roman Empire records.

requiredAdjustments.action: Mention both Rome (500 to 100 BCE) and Roman Republic (400 to 1 BCE) as imported map labels with interleaved snapshots, rather than implying the shared map coverage begins only in 400 BCE.
Replace This phase precedes the map’s Republic coverage with wording stating that this early phase overlaps the Rome label and precedes the Roman Republic label.
Retain the conventional 27 BCE regime transition and distinguish it from both imported end dates. The Rome record ending in 100 BCE is not a historical fall or a separate predecessor state.
Use explicit appliesTo [roman-republic, rome] and the same card path; keep map_coverage date basis. Do not extend this association to Roman Empire or overwrite polygon coordinates.

scopeNotes: The tiny Latium feature at 500 BCE is compatible with the early republican core; Cambridge describes Rome around 509 BCE as a city in Latium. Exact foundation year remains approximate.

Central Italian and later Italian/Iberian expansion is consistent with republican history. A bounding box is insufficient to certify exact sovereignty over all enclosed territory, especially Rome200BCE longitude -7.01; keep this as an imported geometry limitation.

The 46 BCE coin sample and other late Republican examples follow the Rome label’s 100 BCE endpoint but belong to the same continuing polity. The shared card is a diachronic narrative; dated objects must retain their dates.

sourcesChecked.finding: Early republican Latium and growth to control of peninsular Italy by 264 BCE; later literary evidence is uncertain.
Republican government from traditional 509 BCE; expansion beyond Italy and eventual civil-war transition.
27 BCE Augustus settlement supplies conventional distinction from imperial phase.
